To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the displacement efficiency of a buoyancy-dominated displacement flow in a near-horizontal channel can be significantly improved with the use of a highly viscous displacing Newtonian fluid.

the efficiency of a buoyancy-driven displacement flow of two viscous fluids in a near-horizontal channel depends on the relative viscosities of the two fluids, the yield stresses, the inclination angle, and the rheology of the two fluids.

there is a short-time similarity regime, where the interface propagates as a counter-current, that there is a long-time similarity regime, that the number of fronts is a function of the viscosity ratio and other rheological parameters, that yield stress in the fluid being displaced can lead to a residual static layer and that a yield stress in a fluid being injected can increase its displacement efficiency
In summary, our research is concerned with
the displacement of a shear-thinning fluid by a shear-thinning displacing fluid in a near-horizontal channel when buoyancy is important.
the displacement of one fluid by another in a channel inclined at a small angle to the horizontal.
the effects of buoyancy and rheology on the efficiency of miscible displacement flows in near horizontal channels and the associated interface propagation problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the more viscous fluid is displaced by the less viscous fluid, and the less viscous displacing fluids are displaced by the more viscous fluids, provided that the displaced fluid is not too viscous and/or too shear-thinning and/or has a yield stress.
a more viscous, shear-thinning displacing fluid with modest positive inclination and a yield stress in both fluids leads to the most efficient displacement.

the more viscous fluid displaces the less viscous fluid more efficiently, and the more shear-thinning the displacing fluid is, and the more yield stress the displaced fluid has, then the more efficient the displacement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the displacement efficiency is generally improved by using a more viscous fluid, but the efficiency can be increased even more by using a more shear-thinning displacing fluid.
the displacement efficiency is increased by a more viscous fluid and a more shear-thinning displaced fluid, with the latter being particularly effective.
the displacement efficiency is generally enhanced by viscosity and shear thinning of the displacing fluid, and by a yield stress in this fluid, and by slight inclinations in the direction of gravity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the efficiency of miscible displacement flows can be significantly enhanced by using a more viscous fluid as the displacing fluid and a more viscous and less yield-stress-like fluid as the displaced fluid.

, for a given set of rheological and density parameters, the optimal displacement efficiency is obtained when the displacing fluid is more viscous than the displaced fluid, and that a small inclination in the direction opposite the density difference may be used to further improve the displacement efficiency.
, in the presence of buoyancy, the flow is not necessarily driven by the viscosity of the fluids but rather by the competition between viscosity, buoyancy, and rheological effects.
